body.statement: For every exact dyadic triple \((\widetilde X,\widetilde R,\widetilde C)\) in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}^{n^2+2n}\), every real triple \((X,R,C)\) in its coordinate box of radius \(2^{-p_n-1}\), and exact dyadic controls or certified dyadic control intervals of length at most \(L_n\), there is a working precision \(q_n\) bounded by a polynomial in \(n,L_n,p_n,\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\) such that \(H_n^{\mathrm{cert}}\) terminates in bit complexity polynomial in the same quantities and returns \(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}}\) containing the exact-real interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\). The certificate gives \(0\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{dyad}})-\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C))\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})\), remains valid for repeated retained singular values, computes outward enclosures of \(\Phi^{-1}\) and \(F_{\chi^2_{2r}}^{-1}\) in certified polynomial time, returns the bounded outward fallback hull whenever the spectral gate is uncertain, and never silently accepts overflow, a subnormal value, or flush-to-zero behavior.
body.justification: This isolates the arithmetic obligation from probability by asking for a worst-case enclosure theorem on bounded exact dyadic data and explicit real preimage boxes.
body.gap: Verified SVD results do not jointly certify pseudoinverse propagation, discontinuous gate logic, normal and chi-square quantiles, and exceptional floating-point states with polynomial bit complexity.
body.consumer: Interval-library implementers obtain a deterministic certificate that can be audited independently of the panel sampling model.
